findings.problem: The editor panel declares `background: var(--back)` and then `background: var(--fore-06)` four lines later in the same rule; the second wins, so the panel's ground computes to rgba(255,255,255,0.06) and the measure reads straight through it. Driving owner-editing at 1440 I count 13 pairs of text boxes overlapping by more than 4px in both axes: 'Final dress fitting' (24px sans) sits across '−7' and '−1' and across 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days' with a 347px horizontal and 14px vertical overlap; 'Choose the evening music' lies across the 'WHAT GUESTS SEE' micro-label (486px of overlap); 'SAT 29 AUG' runs through 'On the plan' and 'Kept private'; 'Final guest numbers' runs through 'Done' and 'Take it off the plan'. Two type layers superimposed on one line is the single worst thing a type system can do, and it is present at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440. The code comment above the rule promises 'an opaque ground so nothing reads through', so this is a plumbing slip, not a decision — but it is on screen in the state the owner spends the most time in.
findings.fix: In `.b-edit`, delete the second `background: var(--fore-06);` and paint the tint over an opaque ground instead: `background-color: var(--back); background-image: linear-gradient(var(--fore-06), var(--fore-06));`. Keep `z-index: 2`. Then re-run the owner-editing state at 390/768/1280/1440 and assert zero text-box intersections between elements inside `.b-edit` and elements outside it — add that as an assertion in interaction-check.mjs so it cannot come back.

findings.element: .b-when, .b-ogDate, .b-behindNote — print at 1280/1440, phone at 390, the unfurl card
findings.problem: 'Saturday 3 October 2026' — the most ceremonial line in the product — breaks into a 260px line and a 73px line, leaving '2026' alone on the second line. Measured in owner-flight@390, owner-editing@390, desk@390, print@390, print@1280 and print@1440: the printed keepsake orphans the year at every desk width, and so does the phone. The share card does it too ('DAYS TO SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER / 2026', 209px then 32px at 390). '.b-behindNote' widows 'going ahead.' (332px then 87px) at every single width, and '.b-pressBody' ends on a 153px orphan line at 768 and above. There is no widow or balance control anywhere in b.css — no `text-wrap`, no non-breaking spaces — so every one of these is luck, not setting.
findings.fix: Emit the day string with non-breaking spaces between month and year and between the day figure and the month ('Saturday\u00a03\u00a0October\u00a02026' → breaks only after 'Saturday') in fixture.js's date formatter, and add `text-wrap: balance` to `.b-when`, `.b-emptyTitle`, `.b-pressTitle`, `.b-endedTitle`, `.b-dayNames` and `.b-ogDate`, plus `text-wrap: pretty` to `.b-sub`, `.b-gapNote`, `.b-behindNote`, `.b-pressBody`, `.b-emptyBody`, `.b-endedBody` and `.b-note`. Then assert in interaction-check.mjs that no multi-line block's last line rect is narrower than 30% of its first.

findings.problem: The lock declares a 13-step size ramp, a radius ladder, a duration ladder — and no tracking ladder, so tracking has been set per component and has sprawled. Across the eleven states the 11px uppercase Geist Mono micro-label, which is the whole house register, renders with five different letter-spacings: 0.99px, 1.21px, 1.43px, 1.76px and 2.2px (0.09 / 0.11 / 0.13 / 0.16 / 0.20em), 511 instances in total. At 12px there are two more (0.16em and 0.30em). It is visible in one frame: on owner-flight, 'SAT 1 AUG' (0.11em) sits directly above 'SHOWN' (0.09em) and directly below 'DAYS AWAY' (0.16em) — three rhythms in three stacked lines of the same face at the same size. The sans has the same problem: 'Saturday 3 October 2026' is 20px/-0.015em in the phone horizon and 20px/normal on the day card — the same string, the same size, two trackings — and the two 48px/600 headings track differently (-0.03em on the publish title, -0.035em on the day names). A studio's system has two or three tracking steps and reuses them.
findings.fix: Declare a tracking ladder next to the type ramp in shell.css and in lock.md: `--track-label: 0.16em` (all uppercase mono at 11-12px), `--track-data: 0` (mono figures and dates), `--track-body: 0` (sans 13-20px), `--track-head: -0.025em` (sans 24-38px), `--track-display: -0.045em` (sans/mono 48px and up). Replace every hand-set `letter-spacing` in b.css with one of these five, set `.b-dayDate` to the same token as `.b-when`, and add the ladder to audit.mjs so a sixth value fails the gate the way a fourteenth ramp step already does.

findings.problem: Driving the steppers: the readout opens as 'Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days' (347px wide) and on the first press of any of the four steppers it becomes 'in 24 days' (99px) — and it never shows the date again, whichever direction you go afterwards. So the one control whose purpose is to set a date drops the date the instant it is used, the fact changes grammar under the reader (weekday-date-plus-distance becomes distance-only), and a 347px line collapses to 99px mid-panel every time. Separately, the reversibility line sets its number in words — 'the invitations moved seven days closer' — while every other count on every surface is a figure ('in 23 days', '79', '16', 'SAT 22 AUG'); the same string also persists unchanged after a one-day move, so it is not derived from what happened.
findings.fix: In render-b.js, make the readout one template used for every render — `${weekdayLong} ${d} ${monthLong} ${year} · in ${n} days` (and 'tomorrow' / 'today' for n≤1) — built from the same accessor after every step, so its grammar and its width never change. Set the undo sentence from the same accessor with figures, not words: 'Last change: Send the invitations moved 7 days closer.' Keep both on `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so the figures do not jitter as they change.

findings.problem: Everything in the horizon column has a box left edge of exactly 186px at 1440 — but ink is what a reader sees, and the ink does not agree. Measured with actualBoundingBoxLeft after fonts.ready: the 148px Geist Mono '79' starts 8px right of the box (5px at 96px), while 'Saturday 3 October 2026' starts 1px in and the 11px mono labels start at 0. The largest object on the page, the object the whole composition is built around, is the only thing hanging out of the one column this layout has, and the offset drifts between 5px and 8px depending on the leading digit as the countdown ticks. The same class of error sits inside every owner row: `.b-grab` carries `padding: 0 8px`, so 'SHOWN' begins 8px right of the title and date above it — three ragged left edges inside one item, on a surface whose only structure is alignment.
findings.fix: Add `margin-left: -0.05em` to `.b-num` and `.b-ogNum` (7.4px at 148px, 4.8px at 96px, matching the measured ink offsets), or set the count in Geist with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, whose ink offset is 2px and near-constant across digits — both stay inside the locked families. For the row control, change `.b-grab` to `padding: 0; margin: 0` with the hit area restored by `min-height: 28px` plus a `::before { position:absolute; inset:-6px -8px }` overlay, so the word starts on the same left edge as the title and the date.

biggestWin: The register itself. Two families, two weights, one accent and no colour at all doing hierarchy work — and it holds across eleven states because the ramp is genuinely ranged: an 11px uppercase Geist Mono micro-label, 15/17px Geist prose at 400, 24-30px for the day, and a 148px mono count that is allowed to be the entire composition. The count carries the meaning, the mono labels carry the machine facts, the sans carries the human sentences, and the difference between 'this one' and 'the rest' is a filled tick and a jump from 400 to 600 rather than a colour or a chip. Every figure that can change under a reader is on tabular numerals, so nothing reflows as it counts down. On the desk and print frames that reads as a real house style rather than a set of components, and it is the part of this work Home, Notes and Tasks could wear tomorrow.
